scope: Common application work, native Rust and optional modern C++ CBOR versus original C++ binary protocol; no bridge. Same frozen client, 64 cyclic 1027-byte CBOR byte-string values (1024 application bytes), 16-message windows, 64 private pairs and 8192 idle rooms. Original C++ treats values as opaque; both current implementations validate CBOR. Each case runs fresh in a private net namespace, sequentially, pinned to the same server CPU set with client cores separate. Worker/library/build configuration is recorded in cpp_build; active listeners/threads checked for rebuilt C++. Case fanout: no private pairs, one publisher and 63 readers. Case private: only private traffic. Case churn: private traffic plus fixed-room reconnect workers; every welcome, self delivery, Close/EOF checked, and C++ retired member counts verified before its first 30s GC. Case query: private traffic plus authenticated channel inspectors at fixed intervals, no churn; names/counts and full replies verified, sorting normalized only for C++ which does not promise it. HTTP management has no C++ counterpart. Setup and cleanup gated outside timing, every normal close counted, Rust counters/bytes/reservations checked. Latencies include client validation and concurrent client tasks, logarithmic percentile bucket upper bounds. RSS sampled at gates, not continuous peak/allocated memory. Server/client CPU covers all mixed work. Plaintext loopback, no TLS, rates/heartbeats off, default Rust queues; not a language-only or production-capacity comparison.
